tagline.text: A long, quiet surf beach in Daet, Camarines Norte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,500 (transport, lessons and meals, rough estimate for a day trip)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Naga Airport (WNP) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL)

children.text: Bagasbas Beach is a gray-sand beach near Daet in Camarines Norte, often called the surfing spot of the Bicol region. Waves suit beginners through intermediates, and beachfront eateries and a village atmosphere round out the visit.
Bagasbas Beach lies on the coast about
4km
north of the center of Daet, the capital of Camarines Norte. Daet is about
342km

from Manila, and the beach is reported to be recognized by the Department of Tourism (DOT) as a local surfing spot. Surf-spot websites list it among the decent surfing breaks in the Philippines, and locally it has long been called the surfing center of Bicol. The village behind the beach is said to have been rice fields in the past; today it is lined with eateries, lodgings and surf shops.

The sand is gray rather than white. The mood differs from the white-sand beaches of the Philippines, but the beach is long and wide, so it is good for walking and jogging, and easy for warming up in front of the waves. The bottom is sand, so there is little risk of scraping on reef, which makes it a good place to learn. According to a surf-spot website, the waves are a beach break that breaks both left and right, they work best when swell comes from the northeast, and they clean up when the wind blows from the southwest. Wave height starts below about
1m
and can rise past 2.5 m, and 3–6 feet is described as ideal for beginners.

On weekdays there are almost no people in the water and a few more surfers appear on weekends, so it suits travelers who find crowded beaches tiring. Besides surfing, some people bodyboard, skimboard and kitesurf. Even if you do not surf, you can sit at a beachfront eatery and watch the waves, mingle with locals out jogging, or bring a volleyball or a frisbee. The Camarines Norte Surfers Association (CNSA) is said to have a surf shack beside the road at the beach entrance, so stop there first if you need lessons or a board rental.

A trip here is fairly simple. You can base yourself in Daet and go back and forth by tricycle, or stay near the beach and alternate surf lessons with rest. It is also often combined with the nearby Calaguas Islands, the Siete Pecados islands of Mercedes, and Caramoan, as the first base for a northern Bicol trip. This is not a beach for clear turquoise island water; it is a place to enjoy the waves together with the daily life of the village. Simple lodgings and beachfront eateries suit it better than glamorous resorts, and companions who do not surf can read or stroll without getting bored. An airport is reported to be close behind the beach, but regular service could not be confirmed, so plan flights around Naga Airport.

The waves break both left and right over a sandy bottom, which makes it a good place for beginners to practice. On days when the waves are small, first-timers can try standing up many times. Conditions vary a great deal from day to day, so watch the waves from the beach for a while before going in.
Some operators on the beach rent an instructor and a board together. One travel guide lists about

for one hour including instructor and board, but amounts differ between sources and some information is old, so confirm locally. If you bring your own board you can save on rental, and a rash guard is worth packing.

The beach is long and has few people on weekdays, which is good for morning and evening walks or jogging. As you walk you will notice surfers, people at the beachfront eateries and village children going about their day.

Restaurants and small eateries line the beach, where you can eat and drink at chairs and tables. Camping is reported to be uncommon, because the eateries provide places to sit. At sunset, surfers who have finished for the day gather over cold drinks.
Besides surfing, people are known to bodyboard, skimboard and kitesurf. On windy days you may see kites in the sky. Confirm locally whether equipment is available for rent.

Daet town is a few minutes by tricycle from the beach. You can visit the Camarines Norte Provincial Capitol, the Museo Bulawan and the Rizal Monument. The Rizal Monument, unveiled on December 20, 1898, is known as the first monument to José Rizal in the Philippines.

blocks.title: A starting point for island trips

children.text: Daet is a gateway to the Calaguas Islands (departing from Vinzons), the Mercedes islands and Caramoan. Adding an island trip before or after your surfing makes good use of the day.

items.title: Surfing day trip
items.subtitle: Arrive in Daet and surf for half a day

children.text: Have breakfast at your lodging in Daet and take a tricycle to the beach. The beach is a few minutes from town.
Watch the waves for a while, then ask at a surf shop about lessons or board rental. The waves are usually cleaner earlier in the day.
Beginners practice the basic stance on the sand with an instructor, then go into the water. Resting after each hour is easier on the body.
Have lunch at a beachfront eatery and rest in the shade. Do not overdo it in the strong midday sun.
Walk the beach, or head to Daet town to see the Provincial Capitol and the Rizal Monument.
A same-day round trip by bus from Manila means very long travel and can be tiring. If possible, stay one night.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night
items.subtitle: Surfing, Daet town and one island

children.text: Arrive in Daet on the first morning, leave your bags at your lodging and head to the beach.
Take a surf lesson and ride waves several times through the afternoon.
Have dinner and unwind at a beachfront eatery at sunset.
On day two, go to Mercedes for Apuao Grande Island among the Siete Pecados islands, or visit the museums in Daet town.
Island trips can be canceled depending on weather and sea conditions, so leave some slack.
Buses run from Manila to Daet. One travel guide lists about
one way, while another lists about
8 hours
with fares starting at ₱550. These vary by company and time of day, so check at the terminal.
From the bus terminal in Daet to the beach you go by tricycle; one guide lists about
one way and a few minutes. Another source gives about
4km
and 10–15 minutes.
There are no direct flights to Daet. A flight from Manila to Naga Airport is reported to take about
1 hour
From Naga to Daet it is 2–3 hours by van (about
) or bus (about
). These fares come from guides, so confirm current fares locally.
See also the Naga City entry.
Between Daet town and the beach, use a tricycle or jeepney.
For island trips you need to travel separately from Daet toward Mercedes Port or Vinzons.

A surf-spot website explains that good waves form when swell comes from the northeast. One travel blog names September through January as the best period while noting that surfing is possible all year. That period overlaps with typhoon season, so large waves can be dangerous for beginners.
The dry months of March–May have clear weather and are good for beach time and island trips, but there may be many days with small waves. When a typhoon is approaching, follow the sea safety notices.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Northeast swell can bring better waves
Good for beach and island trips, but waves may be weak
Waves grow after September, but dangerous when a typhoon approaches

Small resorts and guesthouses stand near the beach, and the lodgings that travel guides list are in Daet town: Pineapple Island Resort, Nathaniel Hotel, Dolor Hotel and D House Hotel, among others. Check conditions and prices by date on a booking site. Beach cottages are listed at about
per night, but they vary with season and facilities.

Meals are at the beachfront eateries or in Daet town. Seafood and Filipino home cooking are the basics, and in Bicol you can easily find spicy dishes made with coconut milk. Many places do not take cards, so withdraw cash in Daet or Naga beforehand.

After surfing you crave salty snacks and cold drinks. Menus and prices differ between beach eateries, so check the price list before you sit down, and look at the freshness of fish and shellfish before ordering. Daet town has Filipino restaurants, bakeries and a small market, good for snacks and souvenirs. Pineapple is known as Daet's signature product, and some travelers time their visit for the Pineapple Festival (Pinyasan), held June 22–26. Festival schedules can change from year to year, so check the latest announcements.
Bring plenty of cash. Most transactions at the beach and in the village are in cash.
Pack a rash guard and sunscreen. Bringing your own board saves on rental.
Before going in, watch the waves and any rip currents from the beach for a good while.
Beginners should practice on a small-wave morning and start with an instructor.
It is quiet on weekdays and a few more surfers appear on weekends. Choose a weekday if you want peace.
If you want to add an island trip, contact the Mercedes tourism office in advance.
Do not leave trash on the beach. There is no entrance fee, but visitors are asked to keep it clean.
Keep your phone and camera in a waterproof pouch.
In typhoon season the waves can suddenly grow and sea safety notices are issued. Decide whether to enter the water according to safety signs and local guidance.
Waves and rip currents change from day to day. Beginners should always go in with an instructor.
The midday sun is strong, so bring a hat and water and watch for dehydration.
Surfboards drift close by, so when swimming avoid the surfers' area.
Prices and facilities differ between sources and much information is old, so confirm locally.
Do not leave valuables on the beach; keep them at your lodging.
A group of islands reached by boat from Vinzons, with white-sand beaches. Allow a day or more including overland travel and boat from Daet.
Limestone islands and beaches in Camarines Sur. A good next stop to combine in a Bicol itinerary.
The gateway city on the overland route to Daet, with an airport and a cathedral.
Seven islands known as the Siete Pecados. Apuao Grande Island is the best known. Ask the Mercedes tourism office about boats.
